summary: MITRE plans to build a local guide to network usage to supplement the Resources Notebook, built in NLS from local users' experience. It outlines the proposed files and says useful information would be sent to the NIC.

plainLanguage.summary: One company will write its own beginner's guide to the network from what its staff learn, and share good bits with everyone.

questions: mitre local guide to network usage
subtitle: A plan to build a practical guide for network users at MITRE based on real-world experience.

tldr.problem: Network users lacked practical guidance on how to access and use remote systems and resources, with existing documentation being incomplete.
tldr.mechanism: MITRE decided to create a detailed, locally-tailored guide to network usage built in NLS, including information about systems, accounts, documentation, login procedures, and usage tips for each remote site.
tldr.outcome: The guide was planned to become operational in December 1971 and would serve as a model for similar efforts across the network.

today: RFC 274 documents an early-1970s effort to create practical user documentation for the ARPA network. It represents a transition from purely technical documentation to user-focused guides based on real experience.

sections.title: The Local Guide Concept
sections.content:
MITRE Corporation announced its plan to create a guide to network usage tailored specifically for its users. Unlike the generic Resources Notebook, this guide would distill practical experience gained by MITRE staff as they experimented with remote network resources.

The guide was targeted at station agents and secretaries who could help other users access network resources and transcribe documents into NLS. The goal was to bridge the gap between technical documentation and practical user needs.
sections.plainLanguage: MITRE's staff wrote down everything they learned about using the network, so other people there could learn faster.

sections.title: Structure and Content
sections.content:
The guide would be built in NLS, the same online system used by the Network Information Center. It would include site-specific files for each remote resource, with a resource locator file serving as a table of contents linking to detailed site descriptions.

Each site file would document subsystems available there, system availability periods, accounts and login information, system charges, documentation references, login procedures, special considerations for different hardware configurations, and user experience notes about reliability and performance.
sections.plainLanguage: For each computer they could reach, the guide explained how to log in, what it costs, when it was working, and what problems people had found.

sections.title: Network-Wide Impact
sections.content:
MITRE coordinated this effort with the National Bureau of Standards, which was undertaking a similar initiative. Both efforts would contribute useful information back to the Network Information Center, enriching the overall Resources Notebook.

Though tailored for MITRE users, the guide was designed to be accessible to other network users through NLS, multiplying its value. The effort became a model for how sites could maintain practical, experience-based documentation of network resources.
sections.plainLanguage: MITRE shared what it learned with other companies, and they helped each other make better guides.

references.text: Contact E. Forman at MITRE for more information.
